related.why: When a lump must not be excised locally

brief.setting: Minor operations, on a skin model
brief.scenario: A 60-year-old man has a pigmented lesion on his forearm that is suspicious for melanoma. Consent has been taken. Instruments, local anaesthetic and sutures are provided.
brief.task: Perform an excision biopsy on the model, talking the examiner through each step, and answer questions.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Mark, anaesthetise, excise full thickness, orientate, close, send.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Shaving or excising too narrowly, or sending the specimen without orientation.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "I'll confirm the patient, the site and the consent before marking."

grid.label: Checks before starting
grid.fail: Starts without confirming patient, site or consent.
grid.pass: Confirms patient, site and consent; checks allergies and anticoagulants; completes the safety checklist.
grid.high: Marks the site with the patient, and checks there's a plan for how results will be given.

grid.label: Marking and margins
grid.fail: Marks too narrow a margin, or plans a shave.
grid.pass: Marks a 2 mm margin around the suspected melanoma, full thickness to include a cuff of fat.
grid.high: Plans an ellipse about three times as long as it is wide, along the relaxed skin tension lines.

grid.label: Local anaesthetic
grid.fail: Injects without checking the maximum dose.
grid.pass: Checks allergy, calculates the maximum dose, aspirates before injecting.
grid.high: Knows both adult maximum doses: lidocaine 200 mg plain, 500 mg with adrenaline. Waits for it to work before incising.

grid.label: Excision
grid.fail: Cuts at an angle or leaves the base in the dermis.
grid.pass: Incises perpendicular to the skin, full thickness into subcutaneous fat, and removes the ellipse.
grid.high: Holds the skin under tension, and handles the specimen only at its ends or with a skin hook to avoid crush.

grid.label: Specimen (safety-critical)
grid.fail: Sends the specimen without orientation, or doesn't send it.
grid.borderline: Sends it for histology but doesn't orientate it.
grid.pass: Orientates with a marking suture, labels it and sends it for histology.
grid.high: Records site, orientation and the clinical question on the request form.

grid.label: Closure
grid.fail: Closes under tension without undermining, or leaves inverted edges.
grid.pass: Achieves haemostasis; interrupted sutures with everted edges and even spacing.
grid.high: Undermines if tight, and chooses a monofilament non-absorbable skin suture or an absorbable subcuticular one.

grid.label: Sharps and aftercare
grid.pass: Disposes of sharps at the point of use; gives wound care and suture removal instructions.
grid.high: Arranges follow-up for histology and explains that further surgery may be needed depending on the result.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Starts marking without checking the patient or site.]

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I'll shave it off level with the skin.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Injects local anaesthetic without checking a maximum dose.]

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Drops the specimen in a pot with no marking suture.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I'll confirm the patient, the site and the consent, check for allergies and anticoagulants, and do the safety checklist.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Marks a 2 mm margin around the lesion.] This is an excision biopsy, so I'll go full thickness, with a cuff of fat.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: No allergies. I've worked out the maximum dose for his weight. [Aspirates, then infiltrates.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Incises perpendicular to the skin, full thickness into fat, removes the ellipse.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Places a marking suture at one end.] Labelled and sent for histology.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Blade into the sharps bin.] I'll give written aftercare advice; the sutures come out at the practice.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I'll confirm his identity, the site with him, and the consent, check allergies and anticoagulants, and do the safety checklist. I'll also make sure there's a clear plan for how he gets his results.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: A 2 mm margin, full thickness with a cuff of fat, as an ellipse about three times as long as it is wide, along the skin tension lines of the forearm.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Lidocaine with adrenaline: the maximum is 500 mg, or 200 mg if plain, and he's well within that. [Aspirates, infiltrates, waits.] Can you feel this as sharp? Good.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Skin under tension, perpendicular incision into fat; lifts the specimen by one end with a skin hook.]

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Marking suture at the superior end, noted on the form with the site and the question: excision biopsy of a suspected melanoma.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Undermines slightly; interrupted monofilament nylon, everted edges.]

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Sharps disposed at point of use.] I'll explain the wound care, and we'll see him in clinic with the histology, as he may need a wider excision depending on the result.

failures.move: Closing a tight wound without undermining.
failures.consequence: Wound tension, dehiscence and a wider scar.
The pathologist can't say which margin is involved.

failures.move: Injecting without checking allergy and anticoagulants.
failures.consequence: Safety-critical: risks anaphylaxis or uncontrolled bleeding.

recovery.line: For a suspected melanoma, it's a 2 mm margin with a cuff of fat.

recovery.when: You're asked the dose and aren't sure
recovery.line: I'd check the product information and calculate the maximum for his weight before injecting.

knowledge.fact: Suspected melanoma: excision biopsy with a 2 mm margin and a cuff of fat; shave biopsy is inappropriate.
Low-risk BCC: 4 mm peripheral margin; primary high-risk BCC: at least 5 mm.
Adult maximum lidocaine dose: 200 mg plain, 500 mg with adrenaline. The preparation in your hand sets the ceiling; calculate for weight in smaller patients.

recall.think: Right patient, right margin, right orientation.
recall.say: "A 2 mm margin, full thickness, with a cuff of fat."
recall.finish: Orientated specimen to histology; results and further plan arranged.

partner.opening: Please excise this lesion on the model, talking me through what you're doing.

reveals.finding: If they ask: patient confirmed, consent signed, no allergies, not anticoagulated, 70 kg.
Watch whether they orientate the specimen.

push.question: What margin, and why?
push.expect: 2 mm with a cuff of fat for a suspected melanoma.

push.question: What's the maximum dose of your local anaesthetic?
push.expect: Lidocaine 200 mg plain, 500 mg with adrenaline (adult maximum).

push.question: What happens after the result?
push.expect: Follow-up for histology; wider excision may be needed.

curveballs.prompt: It's a low-risk BCC instead. Different margin?

curveballs.safeAnswer: A shave loses the depth, which the pathologist needs for staging.
